clue.text: Leisure venues serving dish in kitchens?

parts.note: a bowl is a dish
taken as written
galleys are the kitchens on ships and aircraft

explanation.surface: A question about restaurants that serve a dish straight from the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'kitchens' are ship's galleys, not restaurant kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling alleys are places people visit for recreation, so they are leisure venues.

clue.text: Meal with duke underpinning complaint

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece underpinning another sits below it, so the duke comes second

parts.note: a beef is slang for a grievance or complaint
the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo

explanation.surface: A dinner where a duke props up someone's grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef Wellington is a dish of fillet steak baked in pastry, eaten as a main meal.

clue.text: Turn around almost at the same time as the Spanish

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: when means at the same time as
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone spins round almost in step with a Spaniard.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to pivot or swing round, a synonym for turning around.

clue.text: Perfectly OK at home — before fine and prison

parts.note: in means at home
good means fine
nick is British slang for prison

explanation.surface: A homebody claims all is well before facing a fine and jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'in good nick' means in sound condition, perfectly all right.

clue.text: Gathered there's delight about article on Germany

indicators.note: about means placed around the article

parts.note: glee is delight
an is the indefinite article
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone is gathered to be thrilled by a piece about Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaned means collected bit by bit, a synonym for gathered.

clue.text: One area avoided by poor nautical hothead

indicators.note: poor signals the remaining letters are in bad shape and reordered
avoided by means the letter is left out of the word that follows

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, and only one of the two As goes

explanation.surface: A hothead has no feel for a single stretch of open water.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one A from NAUTICAL to get NUTICAL, which 'poor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic is a wild, reckless person, much like a hothead.

clue.text: Deliver a sermon, taking ages

indicators.note: taking means the clue words take in, or contain, the answer

explanation.surface: A preacher delivers a sermon that takes forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long historical periods, so ages in the sense of epochs.

clue.text: Poor Ross, covered in pigfeed, gets a sponge

indicators.note: covered in means the shuffled name is wrapped by the pig food

parts.note: swill is kitchen waste fed to pigs

indicators.note: poor signals the name is in a bad way and rearranged

explanation.surface: Unlucky Ross is splattered with pig food but is handed a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for Ross, but it signals his name is jumbled (SSRO) before the pig food wraps round it; 'sponge' is a cake, not a bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a rolled sponge cake with jam filling, so a sponge.

clue.text: Marvellous wood hut florist designed

indicators.note: designed means the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A florist has drawn up plans for a wooden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of this world is an idiom for something extraordinary or superb.

clue.text: Standard song from Plant, say?

definitions.meaning: a classic song that never goes out of fashion
a plant that keeps its leaves all year, the question mark marking an example

explanation.surface: A classic song taken from the singer Robert Plant's repertoire.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is both an enduring popular song and a plant that keeps its foliage.

clue.text: Cheers for a multinational organisation employing detective

indicators.note: employing means the organisation takes the detective on, holding him inside

parts.note: taken as written
EU is the European Union
DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A toast to a big international body that hires a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers and adieu are both ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Left in central London company, as agreed

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: W1 is the postcode of central London, read as WI

explanation.surface: A firm has abandoned the heart of London by mutual consent.
explanation.walkthrough: The postcode W1 is read with the digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilco, radio shorthand for 'will comply', confirms an instruction is agreed.

clue.text: Crazy point put to teachers

indicators.note: put to means the point is attached to the end of the teachers

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A mad idea is put before a staff meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Look after large city in Europe

indicators.note: after means the word for look comes behind the size

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, meaning large
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to mind a big European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, a European city.

clue.text: What a journalist might say I have is telling!

parts.note: a reporter might announce 'I'm press'
I've contracts I have

explanation.surface: A journalist boasts about having a story to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling, as in a telling performance, means striking or impressive.

clue.text: Well-read Shakespearean king warned to avoid fight

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

indicators.note: to avoid means the fight is taken out of the following word

parts.note: war is a fight

explanation.surface: A bookish Lear is advised to steer clear of battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned means scholarly or widely read.

clue.text: Tackled a Democrat fully clothed

parts.note: taken as written
dressed means fully clothed

explanation.surface: An American politician tackled the issue fully dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to tackle or deal with it.

clue.text: Millions to be invested in joint stake in fertiliser

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the millions go into the joint stake

parts.note: co- is the prefix for joint, as in co-owner
a post is a stake

explanation.surface: Millions are put into a shared stake in a fertiliser company.
explanation.definitionFit: Compost is decayed organic matter spread to enrich soil, a fertiliser.

clue.text: Brought on popular Italian leader with daughter

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Il Duce was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A well-liked Italian ruler arrives with his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce labour or a reaction is to bring it on.

clue.text: Bits placed inside brown receptacle

indicators.note: inside means the rearranged word sits within the colour

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish brown

indicators.note: placed means the letters are set down in a new order

explanation.surface: Scraps are tipped into a brown container.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustbin is a container for household rubbish, a receptacle.

clue.text: Rock singer's accumulated knowledge with Garland

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge built up over time
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: A rock singer's expertise is paired with the actress Judy Garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garland' wants to be Judy Garland; it is a plain garland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a Rhine rock where, in legend, a siren sang sailors to their doom.

clue.text: Dish or sink found in road

indicators.note: found in means the sinking word lies inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
to sag is to sink

explanation.surface: A dish or a sink is discovered in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian pasta dish.

clue.text: Source of herbs in my American butter

indicators.note: in means the initial goes inside the exclamation

parts.note: gee is an American exclamation like 'my!'

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Herbs flavour some American butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Invites a king on board

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside the letters for steamship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the vessel one is on board
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone invites a monarch to come aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask someone round is to invite them.

clue.text: Animal that falls short of being clever

indicators.note: falls short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: shrewd means clever

explanation.surface: A creature that is not quite smart enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a small mouse-like mammal, an animal.

clue.text: Engineers do better than turning up to transfer plant

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to top is to do better than

explanation.surface: Engineers improve on arriving to move a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to move a plant into a new container.

clue.text: Unfortunately protected by political asylum

indicators.note: protected by means the answer is sheltered within these words

explanation.surface: Sadly, a refugee is shielded by political asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, meaning unfortunately.

clue.text: Bird's car stolen from roundabout

indicators.note: stolen from means the vehicle is removed from the ride

parts.note: a carousel is a fairground roundabout
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird's car has been taken from a traffic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like a traffic junction; it is the fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a thrush-like bird such as the blackbird or ring ouzel.

clue.text: Stars generous with 26?

parts.note: big means generous, as in big-hearted
the dipper is also called the water ousel, the answer to 26

explanation.surface: A star group generous with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Dipper is the North American name for the Plough, a group of stars.

clue.text: Showing a lack of favouritism, did entire sets in a medley

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tennis player played every set in a mixed fashion and stayed impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterested means impartial, with no stake in the outcome.
